authoritative_sources: ICAR - Indian Council of Agricultural Research
ANGRAU - Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University

groundnut_tikka.symptoms: Circular to subcircular dark-brown to black spots surrounded by a bright yellow chlorotic halo on older leaflets.

paddy_blast.symptoms: Spindle-shaped, elliptical lesions with gray-white ash centers and dark-brown margins on leaf blades.

cotton_leaf_curl.pathogen: Cotton Leaf Curl Virus (CLCuV) transmitted by Bemisia tabaci
cotton_leaf_curl.symptoms: Upward or downward cupping of leaves, thick dark-green veins, and downward foliar enations (leaf-like outgrowths).

tomato_early_blight.symptoms: Concentric rings with target-board pattern on lower leaves with dark necrotic zones and yellow surrounding halos.

chilli_anthracnose.symptoms: Sunken circular dark lesions with concentric rings of black acervuli on pods and leaves, leading to twig dieback.

corn_rust.symptoms: Golden-brown to cinnamon-brown powdery pustules scattered on both upper and lower leaf surfaces.

healthy_foliage.symptoms: Vibrant, uniform green chlorophyll pigmentation, intact leaf margins, no fungal pustules or viral vein clearing.

organic_remedies: Foliar spray of 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) at early onset of spots
Spray Panchagavya (30 ml/L) mixed with Pseudomonas fluorescens (5 g/L)
Deep summer ploughing to bury fungal resting spores in crop residue
Foliar spray of fermented sour buttermilk (10%) at 10-day intervals
chemical_treatments: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L or Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1.0 g/L at 15-day intervals
Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 2.0 ml/L for severe late leaf spot infections
Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1.5 ml/L applied with 200 L water/acre
cultural_practices: Maintain 30x10 cm plant spacing for adequate foliar aeration
Avoid late afternoon overhead sprinkler irrigation that keeps leaves wet overnight
Practice 2-year crop rotation with non-host cereals (pearl millet, sorghum)
groundnut_tikka.source: ANGRAU Crop Protection Advisory AG-GN-2024 / ICAR-DGR Junagadh

organic_remedies: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/kg seed before sowing
Foliar spray of cow urine (10%) fermented with Vitex negundo (Vaavili) leaf extract
Apply silicon fertilizers (calcium silicate) to strengthen leaf epidermal cell walls
chemical_treatments: Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L water (most effective blast-specific fungicide)
Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5 ml/L water at early tillering
Kasugamycin 3% SL @ 2.5 ml/L during initial lesion development
cultural_practices: Avoid split overdosing of chemical nitrogen fertilizer during humid overcast weather
Maintain standing water depth of 2-3 cm to reduce drought stress blast susceptibility
Use blast-resistant varieties like MTU 1010, NLR 34449, or BPT 5204 with seed prophylaxis
paddy_blast.source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR) Hyderabad Bulletin 18

cotton_leaf_curl.pathogen: Cotton Leaf Curl Virus (CLCuV) transmitted by Bemisia tabaci
organic_remedies: Erect bright yellow sticky traps (15-20 per acre) at canopy level to monitor and trap whiteflies
Foliar spray of 10,000 ppm cold-pressed Neem oil @ 3 ml/L with soap emulsifier
Release natural bio-predators (Chrysoperla carnea @ 10,000 larvae/acre)
chemical_treatments: Flonicamid 50% WG @ 0.3 g/L or Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.2 g/L targeting adult whiteflies
Pyriproxyfen 10% EC @ 2.0 ml/L to inhibit whitefly nymphal development
Afidopyropen 50 g/L DC @ 2.0 ml/L during initial vector flare-ups
cultural_practices: Uproot and destroy alternate host weeds (Abutilon indicum, Parthenium hysterophorus) along borders
Sow 2-3 barrier rows of maize, sorghum, or pearl millet around the cotton field
Avoid planting late-season cotton adjacent to tomato or okra fields
cotton_leaf_curl.source: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR) Technical Bulletin 2024

organic_remedies: Foliar spray of Trichoderma viride @ 5 g/L with 1% cow milk as organic spreader
Mulch beds with clean paddy straw (5 cm depth) to stop soil rain-splash spores
Spray Bordeaux mixture (1%) at 10-day intervals during wet weather
chemical_treatments: Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1.0 ml/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L
Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 1.0 ml/L at onset of lower leaf spotting
Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L as preventive protective fungicide
cultural_practices: Prune the lower 30 cm foliage touching the soil bed to enhance airflow
Stake plants properly using trellis strings to keep foliage off ground dampness
Follow drip irrigation rather than overhead sprinklers to keep leaf canopy dry

organic_remedies: Seed treatment with Trichoderma harzianum @ 10 g/kg seed before nursery sowing
Foliar spray of ginger + garlic + chilli extract (3%) as broad-spectrum antifungal
Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens (10 g/L) at flowering and fruit-set stages
chemical_treatments: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Pyraclostrobin 20% WG @ 1.0 g/L
Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1.0 ml/L during fruit maturation
cultural_practices: Collect and burn infected twigs and mummified fruits from previous seasons
Provide raised nursery beds with nylon netting to prevent fungal spore drift
Ensure proper field drainage to prevent stagnant root-zone humidity
chilli_anthracnose.source: ANGRAU Chilli Pathology Bulletins / ICAR-IIVR Varanasi

organic_remedies: Foliar spray of fermented cow dung-urine slurry (Jeevamrit) @ 10%
Spray wettable sulfur @ 2.5 g/L early in the morning before heat rises
chemical_treatments: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L applied when first pustules appear on lower leaves
Pyraclostrobin 20% WG @ 1.0 g/L or Azoxystrobin @ 1.0 ml/L
cultural_practices: Plant rust-tolerant commercial hybrids suited for the agro-climatic zone
Early synchronous planting across the village cluster to prevent late spore transfer
corn_rust.source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR) Ludhiana

organic_remedies: Continue standard prophylactic organic booster sprays (Panchagavya 3% or Jeevamrit)
Conduct weekly field scouting checking 20 representative plants across an acre
Ensure balanced soil organic matter with well-rotted Farm Yard Manure (FYM)
chemical_treatments: No chemical fungicides or insecticides required at this healthy stage
cultural_practices: Maintain scheduled micro-irrigation and clean bund management to prevent weed hosts
